title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Each Executive and senior manager of the Company. Subject to the trading window, the 5-business-day pre-announcement prohibition, any Board-imposed embargo, and the prior written notification requirement.

tiers.name: Directors, Executives and employees
tiers.description: All Directors, Executives and employees (if any) of the Company; bound by the Insider Trading Policy prohibition on dealing while in possession of price sensitive information. This tier is not expressly stated to be subject to the trading-window and notification provisions of the General Trading Policy, which are addressed only to 'Restricted Persons' (defined as Executives and senior managers).

tiers.name: Associated Parties
tiers.description: Immediate family (including a spouse (or equivalent) or dependent), family company or trust of a Restricted Person.

windows.start_anchor: 5 business days before the announcement of a dividend or any other capital management initiative that might have a material impact on the share price
windows.end_anchor: the announcement of the dividend or capital management initiative

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may from time to time designate further periods of time as a prohibited period, and the Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and their associated parties trading in the Company's shares at any time. Confidentiality of such a designation or embargo is not addressed.

rules.detail: The policy addresses only 'buying and selling' and 'trading' or 'dealing' in the Company's shares; there is no definition of dealing, no mention of derivatives, and no provision sweeping derivative instruments into scope.
No hedging provision or definition anywhere in the document.
Monetisation structures (prepaid forwards, etc.) are not mentioned.
Granting security, charges or liens over shares is not mentioned.
No provision on secured financing arrangements of any kind.
No minimum holding period or short-term dealing restriction.

clearance.approver: Chair of the Board (Company Secretary receives notice and confers with the Chair)
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in the Company's shares, by themselves or their associated parties, prior to such intended dealings. This should be done by written notice to the Company Secretary ... The Chair and the Company Secretary must keep a written record of any information received from Restricted Persons in connection with this policy and any clearance or refusal to grant clearance given under this policy.

exceptions.approver: Chair of the Board (or another Director where the Chair is involved)
exceptions.evidence: the Chair may, at his discretion but subject to this section 1.8, give clearance for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) shares in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so ... 'exceptional circumstances' includes severe financial hardship

exceptions.approver: Chair of the Board (or another Director where the Chair is involved)
exceptions.evidence: 'exceptional circumstances' includes ... a court order (or court enforceable undertaking), or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, to transfer or sell shares in the Company
the sale of sufficient entitlements to allow take up of the balance of the entitlements under a rights issue;
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer or pursuant to a scheme of arrangement implemented in accordance with section 411 of the Corporations Act;
transfers of shares in the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary;

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the shares in the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party;

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the shareholders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

exemption_authority: The Chair (or another Director if the Chair is the applicant) has sole discretion to determine whether exceptional circumstances exist and may give written clearance to sell (not purchase) during a prohibited period, provided there is no inside information, specifying a maximum duration for the clearance. The Board separately has absolute discretion to embargo trading at any time and to designate further prohibited periods, with no stated confidentiality or review mechanism.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This General Trading Policy and the restrictions on trading in shares of the Company set out below applies to each Executive and senior manager (Restricted Persons).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: On a literal reading, Directors are not 'Restricted Persons' and so may fall outside the trading-window, notification and embargo provisions of Section 1 entirely, leaving only the bare insider-trading prohibition in Section 2 to govern a director's funded collar, which is an important threshold ambiguity to resolve with the company before structuring.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no derivatives, hedging, margin lending or secured financing regime
bespoke_clauses.clause: (Absence of any provision on hedging, derivatives, margin lending, security/encumbrance, or secured financing anywhere in the document.)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Nothing in this policy expressly or impliedly prohibits an OTC put/call collar or a loan secured over the shares; the only constraints are the overriding statutory and policy bar on dealing while possessing inside information, the narrow 5-day blackout, any ad hoc Board embargo, and (for Restricted Persons) the prior written notification obligation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and their associated parties are prohibited (unless otherwise agreed to by the Board) from dealing in shares during the five business days before the announcement of a dividend or any other capital management initiative that might have a material impact on the share price.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX trading policies, there is no standing blackout tied to half-year or full-year results, so a collar's execution, unwind or roll window is far less constrained by fixed dates, subject only to the 5-day dividend/capital-management window and any discretionary embargo.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and their respective associated parties trading in the Company's shares at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This open-ended, undated embargo power (with no stated confidentiality or duration limit) could still freeze execution or unwind of a collar at any time at the Board's discretion, even though it is not tied to a specific event.

summary: This is a bare-bones policy that contains no provision on derivatives, hedging, monetisation, margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing, so nothing in the document itself prohibits an executive from entering an OTC put/call collar or granting security over vested shares to a bank. The only substantive constraints are the overriding prohibition on dealing while in possession of inside information, a narrow 5-business-day blackout before dividend or capital management announcements, any ad hoc embargo the Board chooses to impose, and, for 'Restricted Persons' (defined only as Executives and senior managers), a prior written notification to the Company Secretary before dealing. Because Directors are not expressly captured by the definition of 'Restricted Persons' in Section 1, it is unclear whether the trading-window and notification regime applies to a director at all, as opposed to only the general insider-trading prohibition in Section 2; this threshold question should be clarified with the company before structuring. Subject to resolving that ambiguity and observing the blackout/embargo and notification steps, a funded collar appears possible, though the bank should not rely on the document for any protection regarding forced-sale mechanics, minimum shareholding, or disclosure of the financing, none of which are addressed.
